email.body:
NOON REPORT - MV TORMAR SPRING
Date/time: 26 Jan 2025 1200 (ship's time UTC)
Position: 50-50.2N 031-32.2W
Distance run last 24h: 231.3 nm
Average speed last 24h: 12.5 kn
ROB VLSFO: 1019.0 t
ROB MGO: 94.5 t
Consumption last 24h: VLSFO 18.8 t, MGO 0.1 t
Next port: Sept-Iles
ETA Sept-Iles: 2025-01-31 1100 UTC
ETA based on: 12.5 kn
Remarks: Main engine stopped 0610-1140 UTC. 0610-0900 drifting on charterers' instructions, awaiting voyage orders. Orders received 0900; on restart the main engine air start valve was found defective, repaired, engine restarted 1140 and passage resumed. Average speed over 18.5 h steaming. Fuel used: VLSFO 0.6 t while drifting 0610-0900, VLSFO 0.5 t during repair 0900-1140 (generators and boiler).

Master MV TORMAR SPRING

result.result:
The Master's ETA is consistent with the ship's position and speed. No ETA notice is due at this time.

The main engine stop (06:10-11:40 UTC) agrees with the report. Based on the charter party terms, only the period from 09:00 to 11:40 UTC (due to the defective air start valve) is off-hire; the preceding period (06:10-09:00 UTC) was on charterers' instructions and remains on hire. For the off-hire period (2.67 hours), the simulated hire statement shows a hire deduction of 1,055.56 USD and bunkers for the owners' account of 300 USD (0.5 t VLSFO), totaling 1,355.56 USD. The operator should decide whether to put the ship off hire for this period and notify the owner. If agreed, this would involve (a) a voyage management system entry for the off-hire period and (b) an e-mail to the owner's vessel technical management providing the period and reason, and requesting the engine log extract.
